title: A tree stored in an array
summary: A complete binary tree needs no pointers: the children of cell i are cells 2i+1 and 2i+2.

checkpoints.text: Seven values in an array. Below it, the same values are drawn as a tree, level by level: cell 0 is the root, cells 1 and 2 are the next level, cells 3 to 6 the one after.
The children of cell 1 (30) are cells 2 × 1 + 1 = 3 and 2 × 1 + 2 = 4: 10 and 20. No pointers are stored; the positions are worked out with arithmetic.
Going up instead: the parent of cell 6 is (6 - 1) / 2 = 2, using integer division.
One more step up: the parent of cell 2 is cell 0, the root.
This only works because the tree is complete: every level is full except maybe the last, which fills from the left, so there are no gaps in the array. A heap is always a complete tree.
